[LDET.1.10] **One version, and it is the DS version.** No DS artefact carries a
format version of its own. A `.dsc` records the version that compiled it, in
`proto/header.proto#DscHeader`'s `compiler_version`; a `.dstrace` records the
version that wrote it, in `proto/stream_header.proto#StreamHeader`'s
`ds_version`. There is no second version axis, and a runtime **must not**
introduce one.

**The acceptance rule is a string prefix on the minor series.** A runtime
**must** accept an artefact whose recorded version begins with its own
`<major>.<minor>.` and **must** reject every other — a `.dsc` with
`DS_ERR_DSC_VERSION`, a `.dstrace` with `DS_ERR_FS_VERSION` ([NERR.13]). A `0.12.4` runtime therefore reads what `0.12.0` and
`0.12.9` wrote and refuses everything from `0.11` and `0.13`. The comparison is
on the string, so it needs no parse and admits no ordering question: a version
either shares the prefix or it does not.

**[LDET.1.1]'s guarantee is scoped to that series.** One event trace replayed
against one compiled rule set produces the same observable output for every
release sharing a `<major>.<minor>.` prefix. Across a minor bump the guarantee
does not hold, and nothing claims it does — replaying a historical recording
requires the release that wrote it ([RARC.4.2]).

**Why one number is enough.** Protobuf is normative specification here, not an
implementation detail ([STYL.2.14]): the wire shapes **are** part of the
language definition, so they move when the language moves and at no other time.
A version derived from the release therefore changes exactly when the wire can
change.

**The cost, stated because it binds work rather than prose.** A change to what
bytes mean **must not** land inside a minor series: recordings made earlier in
that series would stop replaying identically, which is the guarantee above. Wire
changes wait for the minor bump.

⚠ **`proto/header.proto#DscHeader` and `proto/stream_header.proto#StreamHeader`
carry no format version.** The field numbers and names they reserve are out of
use: nothing may read them, and they are never reused ([STYL.2.8.7]).
